title: A Home Office
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who started working from home. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man was told by his boss that he could work from home.
scenes: コマ1:上司が男性に「来月から在宅勤務でいい」と伝え、男性が喜んでいる。
コマ2:「The next weekend」。男性が家具店で机と椅子を選んでいる。
コマ3:「A month later」。男性が自宅の部屋でオンライン会議をしているが、後ろで子どもたちが騒いでいる。
コマ4:「That evening」。男性が妻と、共有ワークスペースの広告を見ながら話し合っている。
narrationSample: One day, a man was told by his boss that he could work from home starting the following month. He was very happy to hear this. The next weekend, he went to a furniture store and chose a desk and chair for his home office. A month later, he was having an online meeting in his room, but his children were making a lot of noise behind him. That evening, he and his wife were looking at an advertisement for a shared workspace and discussing whether he should use it.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Working from home is convenient, but it's hard to concentrate with the kids around. Using a shared workspace a few days a week might be a good solution."

questions.question: Do you think more companies will allow their employees to work from home in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Online meeting tools have improved a lot, and many workers want a better work-life balance. Companies can also save money on office space.

questions.question: Should companies provide money to help employees set up home offices?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes. If companies ask employees to work from home, they should help pay for desks, chairs, and internet costs. This would also help employees work more efficiently and stay healthy.

title: A Community Clean-Up
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a girl who was concerned about litter in her town. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a girl was walking along the river near her house.
scenes: コマ1:女の子が川沿いを歩いていて、ペットボトルやごみが落ちているのを見て悲しそうにしている。
コマ2:「The next day」。女の子が学校で先生に、清掃活動のポスターを見せて相談している。
コマ3:「That Sunday」。生徒や近所の人たちが一緒に川辺のごみを拾っている。
コマ4:「A week later」。女の子が同じ川辺で、また誰かがごみを捨てているのを見て困った顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a girl was walking along the river near her house. She was sad to see plastic bottles and other trash lying everywhere. The next day, she showed her teacher a poster for a clean-up event and asked for advice. That Sunday, many students and neighbors gathered and picked up trash along the river together. A week later, however, the girl was at the same place, and she saw someone throwing away trash again. She looked troubled.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the girl, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Cleaning up is not enough. We need to make people aware of the problem. Maybe we could put up signs or ask the town to install more trash cans."

questions.question: Do you think young people today are interested in volunteer activities?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think many young people are interested, but they are busy with school and part-time jobs. If there were more short and flexible volunteer opportunities, more young people would participate.

questions.question: Should people who throw away trash on the street be fined?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Fines would make people think twice before littering. However, the government should also provide enough trash cans so that people have a place to throw away their garbage.

title: Learning to Cook
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a young man who lived alone. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a young man was eating convenience store food alone in his apartment.
scenes: コマ1:一人暮らしの若い男性がアパートでコンビニ弁当を食べながら、健康診断の結果を見て心配そうにしている。
コマ2:「That weekend」。男性が料理教室に申し込んでいる。
コマ3:「A few weeks later」。男性が料理教室で、ほかの参加者と楽しそうに野菜を切っている。
コマ4:「One evening」。男性が自宅で料理を作りすぎてしまい、大量の料理を前に困っている。
narrationSample: One day, a young man was eating convenience store food alone in his apartment. He looked at the results of his health checkup and became worried. That weekend, he signed up for a cooking class. A few weeks later, he was enjoying cutting vegetables with the other people in the class. One evening, he cooked dinner at home, but he made far too much food. He looked at all the dishes and didn't know what to do.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the young man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I made too much food. I should invite some friends over to eat it, or freeze the rest for later. Next time, I'll plan my portions more carefully."

questions.question: Do you think schools should teach more practical skills such as cooking?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Many young people don't know how to cook healthy meals when they start living alone. Learning basic cooking skills at school would help them stay healthy and save money.

questions.question: Some people say that convenience stores have made people's eating habits worse. What do you think about that?
questions.sampleAnswer: I partly agree. Many people eat convenience store food every day, and it often contains a lot of salt and fat. However, convenience stores now sell healthier products, such as salads, so it depends on what people choose.

title: A Shop's New Idea
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who owned a small bakery. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One evening, a woman was closing her small bakery.
scenes: コマ1:パン屋の女性が閉店時、売れ残ったたくさんのパンを見てため息をついている。
コマ2:「The next day」。女性がスマートフォンで、売れ残り食品を安く売るアプリに登録している。
コマ3:「A month later」。閉店前に、アプリで予約した客たちが店の前に並んでいる。
コマ4:「One morning」。女性が店を開けると、朝の通常の客がほとんどいなくて困っている。
narrationSample: One evening, a woman was closing her small bakery, and she sighed when she saw a lot of unsold bread. The next day, she registered with a smartphone app that sells leftover food at a discount. A month later, many customers who had made reservations through the app were lining up in front of her shop before closing time. One morning, however, when she opened the shop, there were very few customers. She was worried because people seemed to be waiting to buy cheap bread in the evening.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Customers are waiting until the evening to buy bread at a discount. I should reduce the amount I sell through the app and make special products that are only available in the morning."

questions.question: Do you think food waste is a serious problem in Japan?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes. A lot of food is thrown away by stores and households every day, even though it is still safe to eat. This wastes resources and increases greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.question: Should supermarkets be required to donate unsold food to people in need?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it's a good idea. Supermarkets could reduce waste, and people who cannot afford enough food would benefit. However, the government should help with the cost of transporting and storing the food.

title: A Hiking Trip
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a couple who liked hiking. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a couple was planning a hiking trip at home.
scenes: コマ1:夫婦が自宅で山の地図を広げて、ハイキングの計画を立てている。
コマ2:「The next Saturday」。夫婦が山道を歩いているが、空が暗くなり始めている。
コマ3:「An hour later」。激しい雨の中、夫婦が山小屋に避難している。
コマ4:「A week later」。夫婦が登山用品店で、雨具と携帯ラジオを買っている。
narrationSample: One day, a couple was looking at a map of the mountains and planning a hiking trip at home. The next Saturday, they were walking along a mountain path, but the sky began to get dark. An hour later, it was raining heavily, and the couple took shelter in a mountain hut. A week later, they went to an outdoor shop and bought rain gear and a portable radio so that they would be better prepared next time.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the wife, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "We were lucky to find that hut last week. With this rain gear and radio, we'll be safer next time. We should also check the weather forecast more carefully before we leave."

questions.question: Do you think outdoor activities are becoming more popular in Japan?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Many people want to relax in nature after spending long hours in front of screens. Camping and hiking also became popular as activities that people can enjoy safely with small groups.

questions.question: Should people who need to be rescued in the mountains because of poor preparation pay for the rescue?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think they should pay part of the cost. Rescues are expensive and can put rescuers in danger. If people had to pay, they would prepare more carefully. However, the fee should not be so high that people hesitate to ask for help.

title: A New Neighbor
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about an elderly woman who lived alone. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, an elderly woman saw a family moving into the house next door.
scenes: コマ1:一人暮らしの高齢女性が、隣の家に外国人の家族が引っ越してくるのを窓から見ている。
コマ2:「The next day」。女性が手作りのお菓子を持って隣の家を訪ね、家族と笑顔であいさつしている。
コマ3:「A few weeks later」。隣の家の子どもが女性の家で日本語の宿題を教わっている。
コマ4:「One day」。女性が家の中で転んで動けず、隣の家族が心配して駆けつけている。
narrationSample: One day, an elderly woman who lived alone saw a family from another country moving into the house next door. The next day, she visited them with some homemade sweets, and they greeted each other with smiles. A few weeks later, the family's child was at the woman's house, and she was helping the child with Japanese homework. One day, the woman fell down in her house and could not get up. The family next door noticed and rushed over to help her.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm so lucky to have such kind neighbors. If I hadn't become friends with them, nobody would have found me. I should thank them properly."

questions.question: Do you think relationships between neighbors are weaker than in the past?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so, especially in cities. Many people are busy and don't even know who lives next door. However, local events and online community groups can help people get to know each other.

questions.question: Should the government do more to support elderly people who live alone?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes. The number of elderly people living alone is increasing, and some of them are lonely or have trouble in emergencies. The government could provide regular visits or devices that alert family members when something is wrong.

title: A Library Event
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a librarian in a small town. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a librarian noticed that very few people were visiting the library.
scenes: コマ1:町の図書館で、司書の男性ががらんとした館内を見て困っている。
コマ2:「The next week」。司書が同僚と、子ども向けの読み聞かせ会とボードゲーム大会の企画を話し合っている。
コマ3:「A month later」。図書館に家族連れが大勢集まり、読み聞かせ会が盛り上がっている。
コマ4:「After the event」。図書館の床におもちゃや本が散らかっていて、司書が疲れた顔で片付けている。
narrationSample: One day, a librarian in a small town noticed that very few people were visiting the library. The next week, he and his colleague discussed plans for a storytelling event for children and a board game tournament. A month later, many families came to the library, and the storytelling event was a great success. After the event, however, toys and books were scattered all over the floor, and the librarian looked tired as he cleaned up.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the librarian, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "The event was a success, but cleaning up alone is hard. Next time, I'll ask some volunteers to help, or ask families to put things back before they leave."

questions.question: Do you think public libraries are still necessary in the age of the internet?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Libraries provide free access to books and information for everyone, including people who can't afford to buy books. They are also places where people can study and join community events.

questions.question: Should children be encouraged to read more paper books rather than digital books?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think children should read both. Paper books help them concentrate without the distractions of other apps, but digital books are convenient and can include audio. The most important thing is that children enjoy reading.

title: Saving Energy at Home
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a family that wanted to reduce its electricity bill. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a father was surprised when he saw the family's electricity bill.
scenes: コマ1:父親が高額な電気料金の請求書を見て驚いている。
コマ2:「That evening」。家族会議で、父親が「使わない電気は消す」「エアコンの温度を調整する」と書いた紙を見せている。
コマ3:「The next month」。家族が屋根にソーラーパネルを付ける業者の説明を聞いている。
コマ4:「The following summer」。暑い部屋で、エアコンを控えている家族が汗をかいてぐったりしている。
narrationSample: One day, a father was surprised when he saw the family's high electricity bill. That evening, he held a family meeting and showed everyone a list of ideas, such as turning off lights that were not being used and adjusting the temperature of the air conditioner. The next month, the family listened to a company's explanation about installing solar panels on their roof. The following summer, however, the family members were sweating in a hot room because they were trying not to use the air conditioner. They all looked exhausted.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the father, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Saving energy is important, but it's dangerous not to use the air conditioner when it's this hot. Our health is more important than the electricity bill."

questions.question: Do you think people in Japan are making enough effort to save energy?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think many people try to save energy, but there is still room for improvement. For example, many stores and offices use too much air conditioning, and homes could be better insulated.

questions.question: Should the government require all new houses to have solar panels?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it's a good idea in principle because it would increase the use of renewable energy. However, solar panels are expensive, so the government should provide financial support so that the rule doesn't make houses too expensive.

title: A Language Exchange
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a college student who wanted to improve her English. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a college student was studying English vocabulary in the library.
scenes: コマ1:女子大学生が図書館で英単語帳を見ているが、英会話ができずに悩んでいる様子。
コマ2:「The next week」。学生が大学の掲示板で「言語交換パートナー募集」の貼り紙を見つける。
コマ3:「A month later」。学生が留学生とカフェで、英語と日本語を教え合っている。
コマ4:「A few months later」。学生が空港で、帰国する留学生と別れを惜しんでいる。
narrationSample: One day, a college student was studying English vocabulary in the library, but she was worried because she couldn't speak English well. The next week, she found a notice on the university bulletin board looking for language exchange partners. A month later, she was at a café with an international student, and they were teaching each other English and Japanese. A few months later, she went to the airport to say goodbye to the international student, who was returning to her home country. They were both sad to part.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the college student, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'll miss her a lot. Thanks to her, my English has improved so much. Let's keep in touch online, and someday I'd like to visit her country."

questions.question: Do you think studying abroad is necessary to become good at English?
questions.sampleAnswer: No, I don't think it's necessary. These days, people can practice speaking with native speakers online and watch English videos easily. Studying abroad is helpful, but people can improve a lot at home if they are motivated.

questions.question: Should universities accept more international students?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes. International students bring different perspectives, and Japanese students can learn about other cultures without leaving the country. However, universities need to provide enough support, such as housing and Japanese classes.

title: A Farmers' Market
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a farmer who wanted to sell vegetables directly to customers. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a farmer was looking at the low price he received for his vegetables.
scenes: コマ1:農家の男性が、野菜の買い取り価格の安さに落胆している。
コマ2:「A few days later」。男性が市役所で、週末のファーマーズマーケットへの出店を申し込んでいる。
コマ3:「That weekend」。マーケットで男性が客に野菜の育て方を説明し、客が喜んで買っている。
コマ4:「In the afternoon」。急な雨で客がいなくなり、男性が売れ残った野菜の前で困っている。
narrationSample: One day, a farmer was disappointed when he saw the low price he received for his vegetables. A few days later, he went to the city office and applied to sell his vegetables at a weekend farmers' market. That weekend, he explained to customers how he grew his vegetables, and they were happy to buy them. In the afternoon, however, it suddenly started raining, and the customers left. The farmer looked troubled as he stood in front of his unsold vegetables.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the farmer, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "It's a shame about the rain. Maybe I could start selling my vegetables online too, so that I don't depend only on the market. I could also sell the leftovers to a local restaurant."

questions.question: Do you think people should buy more locally grown food?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Local food is fresh, and buying it supports farmers in our area. It also reduces the energy used to transport food over long distances.

questions.question: Some people say that young people are not interested in agriculture. What do you think about that?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it's partly true because farming is hard work and the income is not stable. However, new technology, such as drones and sensors, is making farming more attractive, and some young people are starting their own farms.

title: A Fitness App
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who wanted to get in shape. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One morning, a man noticed that his pants had become too tight.
scenes: コマ1:男性が朝、ズボンがきつくなっていることに気づいて困っている。
コマ2:「That evening」。男性がスマートフォンでフィットネスアプリをダウンロードしている。
コマ3:「Two months later」。男性が公園で毎朝ジョギングをして、アプリの記録を見て満足している。
コマ4:「One day」。男性が足首を痛めて病院で医師の説明を聞いている。
narrationSample: One morning, a man noticed that his pants had become too tight, and he was worried. That evening, he downloaded a fitness app on his smartphone. Two months later, he was jogging in the park every morning, and he looked satisfied as he checked his records on the app. One day, however, he hurt his ankle and went to the hospital, where a doctor explained that he had been running too much.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I tried too hard to improve my records. I should have rested more. After my ankle gets better, I'll start slowly and maybe try swimming instead."

questions.question: Do you think technology helps people live healthier lives?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Apps and smartwatches make it easy to track exercise and sleep, which motivates people. However, some people rely too much on numbers and forget to listen to their bodies.

questions.question: Should companies give employees time to exercise during working hours?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes. Healthy employees are more productive and take fewer sick days. Even short exercise breaks can reduce stress and help people concentrate, so it would benefit companies too.

title: A School Trip Abroad
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a high school teacher who planned a school trip. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a high school teacher suggested a school trip abroad at a staff meeting.
scenes: コマ1:高校の先生が職員会議で、海外への修学旅行を提案している。
コマ2:「A few months later」。生徒たちが教室で、訪問先の国の文化について調べて発表している。
コマ3:「During the trip」。生徒たちが現地の学校で、現地の生徒と一緒に料理を作っている。
コマ4:「On the last day」。空港で、一人の生徒がパスポートをなくして先生が慌てている。
narrationSample: One day, a high school teacher suggested a school trip abroad at a staff meeting. A few months later, the students were researching the culture of the country they would visit and giving presentations in class. During the trip, the students visited a local school and cooked a meal together with the local students. On the last day, however, one of the students lost his passport at the airport, and the teacher panicked.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the teacher, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I need to stay calm. First, let's check all his bags again, and if we can't find it, we'll contact the embassy. Next time, I'll collect the passports and keep them myself."

questions.question: Do you think high school students should have more opportunities to go abroad?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Visiting another country helps students become more open-minded and motivates them to study foreign languages. Schools and the government should help reduce the cost so that more students can go.

questions.question: Some people say that school trips are too expensive for many families. What do you think about that?
questions.sampleAnswer: I agree that some school trips are very expensive. Schools should choose destinations that are reasonable, and local governments could provide financial support for families who cannot afford the cost.

title: An Old Family Business
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a young woman whose father ran a traditional shop. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a young woman visited her father's traditional tea shop.
scenes: コマ1:若い女性が父親の老舗のお茶屋を訪ね、客が少ないのを見て心配している。
コマ2:「The next week」。女性が父親に、店の商品をネットで販売する計画を説明している。
コマ3:「Six months later」。店に海外からの注文が次々に届き、二人が箱詰めをしている。
コマ4:「One evening」。父親が大量の注文書を前に疲れ切っていて、女性が心配している。
narrationSample: One day, a young woman visited her father's traditional tea shop and was worried to see very few customers. The next week, she explained to her father her plan to sell their products online. Six months later, orders were arriving one after another from overseas, and the two of them were busy packing boxes. One evening, however, the father looked exhausted in front of a large pile of orders, and his daughter was worried about him.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the young woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm glad the online shop is successful, but my father is working too hard. We should hire some part-time workers or limit the number of orders we accept each day."

questions.question: Do you think traditional businesses can survive in modern society?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they can if they adapt. Many people, including tourists, value traditional products. If traditional shops use the internet and social media, they can reach new customers.

questions.question: Should young people take over their family businesses?
questions.sampleAnswer: I don't think they should be forced to. Young people should be free to choose their own careers. However, if they are interested, taking over a family business can be a meaningful way to protect local culture.
